<reason>Side B (PRO) won the two decisive clashes. First, A's central reframe—that fatalities come from dangerous drivers, not speed numbers—was answered by B's kinetic-energy rejoinder (the drunk at 25 goes to the hospital, at 45 to the morgue), which A never defeated, only deflected to coverage. Second, B's certainty-over-severity deterrence frame, reinforced by inverting A's durability test with the 2020 enforcement collapse, beat A's speculative claim that unpredictable mobile patrols generalize compliance. B also handled pressure better: the checkpoint-concession trap was defused cleanly ("bonus, not a dependency," cameras work with zero officers reassigned), and the income-scaling question was answered with real, verifiable jurisdictions (Finland, Switzerland) plus the strong point that flat fines and suspension spirals afflict police tickets identically. A answered pressure honestly ("single digits, at best"), which B leveraged into the memorable "twenty-to-fifty roadside encounters per dangerous driver found" lottery framing in closing. A landed real hits—the surveillance externality persistence, the mapped-corridor coverage gap, the clever checkpoint trap—but B's responses (plate readers already log cars; cameras photograph only when speeding; average-speed corridors) kept those routes contained. Both sides followed format well; both had minor clipping costs. B made the debate easier to decide and controlled the weighing in the final speeches.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>The decisive exchange was A's impairment-blindness attack ("a camera's hit rate on the drunk at the limit is exactly zero") against B's kinetic-energy response in Rebuttal 2 ("the same drunk at twenty-five sends them to the hospital; at forty-five, the morgue")—B converted A's strongest structural point into a concession that cameras reduce the severity of even uncatchable drivers' crashes, while A's honest "single digits" admission let B price the collateral-discovery benefit at tens of thousands of armed encounters per dangerous driver found.</best_rebuttal>
